sentences.text: Eucnemesaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur named for its robust tibiae.
This animal presumably had the typical prosauropod build of a long neck and tail but walked on two legs.
The two species of Eucnemesaurus, E. entaxonis and E. fortis, differ from one another in adaptations of the femur shaft and lower shin band for rear leg support function.
The genus was named in 1920 by Egbert Cornelis Nicolaas van Hoepen based on holotype TM 119, the specimen the species is based on.
Remains were found by Van Hoepen in the Lower Elliot Formation on a farm in Slabberts, South Africa, dating to the Late Triassic.
The genus name derives from the Greek words eu, meaning well-formed, knemè, meaning tibia, and saurus, meaning lizard.
Specimens of Eucnemesaurus vertebrae have been used in recent studies on the development of skeletal pneumaticity in early dinosaur genera.
The genus is classified within the family Riojasauridae.
Riojasauridae were more closely related to sauropods than to Plateosauridae but more basal than Massospondylidae.
They lived during the late Triassic, approximately 225 to 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa.

For many years, the size of the femur led paleontologists to believe Aliwalia was a notably large carnivorous dinosaur for its time. However, the maxilla once assigned to Aliwalia is not distinct from material belonging to Eucnemesaurus and is clearly from a carnivore, suggesting the bone was misidentified.
